Identifiable intangible assets include brand names if they meet the definition of an intangible asset (identifiable, control, future economic benefits) and can be measured reliably. A brand name is typically considered separable (can be sold, transferred, licensed, etc.) and thus identifiable. So the brand should be recognized separately as an intangible asset, not subsumed into goodwill.

However, sometimes a brand can be considered a CGU if it generates cash flows largely independent.
